RULING M1/M2 (fix round M, phase-m1-rulings.md, Blocking — closing review phase-l1-review-value.md's BLOCKING 1 and BLOCKING 2, and phase-l1-review-truth.md). L2 corrected the blank's `unisex`/`audienceLean`/`audienceLeanByDesign`/`mixedFamilies` fields to the record, but left `specFacts` hardcoded (`["Classic Fit","50% Cotton / 50% Polyester"]`) beside the newly-corrected `unisex: true` blank. That hardcoded array is INCONSISTENT with the ONE pad bank the live composer reads, `ihSpecFactFillers` (`src/lib/fba/productDetailAttrs.ts:516-533`, read at `itemHighlightComposer.ts:436`): given this fixture's own blank it derives `["50% Cotton / 50% Polyester","Classic Fit","Unisex Fit"]` — a different order, and one fact (`Unisex Fit`) missing entirely -- its length is pinned in the fixture test and read from that test's own logged output, never hand-typed here (RULING O4). That missing pad fact was the entire difference between the wrongly-reported minority-accept outcome and the honest majority-accept one, on the designs whose best case with the incomplete pad fell just short of the accept floor -- the exact unit count, join length and floor are pinned in the fixture test itself (never retyped here; RULING O4, round O, phase-o1-rulings.md) and read from that test's own logged output, not from this note. `specFacts` is therefore no longer a field this fixture carries at all: the test derives it at run time by calling `ihSpecFactFillers` on the blank below, exactly as the live composer does, so it structurally cannot drift from the blank again (RULING M1's own preferred remedy — 'delete the field and have the test call the producer, which is better, because a derived value cannot drift from the blank the way an invented one just did twice').

THE CORRECTED MECHANISM (RULING M2 — do not describe this as a gender refusal of all six phrases). The pool's gendered phrases ('Embroidered Sweatshirts for Women', 'Sweatshirts for Women Trendy', 'Graphic Crewneck Sweatshirts Women', 'Fall Graphic Sweatshirts for Women', 'Fun Sweatshirts for Women') name a gender and are correctly refused by `phraseTruthVerdict`'s forced-gender rule (contentTruth.ts, field='highlights', ctx.audienceLean==='unisex') for the designs that inherit the family's unisex default -- the exact `truthDrops` count every real composer run logs is pinned in the fixture test (RULING O4) and read from its own logged output, never hand-typed in this note. The SIXTH phrase, 'Fall Crewneck', names no gender, is admitted on every design, and is the pool unit in the rank-1 line of most of the family's designs (it is not a spare) -- the exact count is whatever the fixture test's own run logs, never hand-typed here (RULING O4). Measured end to end through the REAL `produceItemHighlightsPerDesign` on this fixture's own (now-derived) specFacts, the recorded lean, and the recorded live title shape: every design that clears RULING I2's own STOP floor for the family does so -- RULING O4 (round O): which designs, and how many, is pinned in the fixture test's own ACCEPTS_ON_RECORDED_LEAN set and read from that test's own logged output, never named or counted in this note (RULING N3/N4 changed the set from an earlier round's own name-list here; a hand-typed name-list is exactly the class RULING O4 exists to retire, so this note does not carry one at all any more). The one design that ORIGINALLY held (superseded below, RULING N3/N4 and RULING O4), DQG ("Don't Quit"), did not hold on gender: it is the family's shortest design name, and its entire admitted unit multiset fell short of the accept floor by construction, so the bounded search never evaluated a single arrangement. The unit count, the naive-join length and the floor it fell short of -- and, after N3/N4, the corrected values that now clear it -- are pinned in the fixture test (RULING O4) and read from that test's own logged output, never retyped in this note; DQG's CURRENT status (after N3/N4) is likewise read from the test's own log, never hand-typed here. That is a band-vs-design-name-length finding, filed, not a pool-gender one and not a writer defect (memory `unisex-lean-vs-a-women-pool-starves-the-field` still names the correct MECHANISM — a unisex lean against a mostly-gendered pool — but the correct accept COUNT is the one this fixture's own test derives and logs once the pad is derived rather than invented, never the smaller count the memory's own headline was written against; RULING O4 (round O) names hand-typing that count here as the same class of defect).

`titleTemplate` (NEW, RULING M5): the fixture recorded no title text at all, although the title decides the number (a parent title containing both 'Fall' and 'Crewneck' title-dedupes the pool's only ungendered phrase and drops the family's accept count back down — the exact count is whatever the test's own run against that title logs, never hand-typed here (RULING O4)). The value below is the family's own RECORDED live shape (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-05-title-judge-sees-shipped-bytes.md:28-31`, 'siblings correctly read `Sweatshirt | Long Sleeve Pullover Crewneck`'), used by both the per-design test and any future e2e probe — never a hand-invented title constant.

`mixedFamilies` (RULING M5 — decision recorded, not silently dropped): this field matches the record (contentTruth.ts:74, B0DSCDZC6K ships Gildan 18000 sweatshirts AND 18500 hoodies under one parent) and is KEPT here as documentation of that fact. It is NOT fed into the fixture test's own hand-built `truthCtx`, because the live Item Highlights path (`PerDesignItemHighlightsInput` / `buildItemHighlights`, listingPipeline.ts) has NO `mixedFamilies` field at all — review phase-l1-review-value.md IMPORTANT 1 measured that feeding it into the test's ctx alone makes this fixture's oracle judge a garment-noun claim ('pullover hoodie for women') `ok` when the live path would refuse it as `wrong-garment-noun`, i.e. strictly MORE permissive than any line the live path can actually judge. Threading `mixedFamilies` through the real pipeline is a real gap, filed for a future round, not fixed in this one — this fixture states the record without pretending the live path already consumes it.

Everything else K4/L2 sourced is UNCHANGED and remains RECORDED per its own citations: (a) RECORDED: designKeys/designNames — the PO, RULING K4: BB='Business B*tch', BCSG='Billionaire Coming Soon', DQG="Don't Quit", EDG='Entrepreneur Definition', HDG='Hustle Definition', MHG='Mother Hustler'. The LIVE store currently holds two typos the PO is correcting: 'Billionare Coming Soon' (BCSG) and 'Hustle Definiton' (HDG) — this fixture carries the CORRECTED spellings; production listing_content on B0DSCDZC6K may still read the typo'd form until the PO's own correction ships.

(a) RECORDED: pool — verbatim from the PO's own live shadow run (IH_WRITER=shadow, B0DSCDZC6K, 2026-09-23, sha f4317ce), phase-f1-report.md §0: 'Embroidered Sweatshirts for Women', 'Sweatshirts for Women Trendy', 'Graphic Crewneck Sweatshirts Women', 'Fall Graphic Sweatshirts for Women', 'Fun Sweatshirts for Women', 'Fall Crewneck'. This is the family's ONE shared pool (the shadow run named it once, not per design) — every design below is given the SAME six phrases, never a per-design invention.

(a) RECORDED: blank fabric/construction — Gildan 18000, 50/50 (cotton/polyester) crewneck, Classic fit (RULING K4). `material` is written '50% Cotton / 50% Polyester' to match this repo's own spelling convention for a 50/50 blend.

(b) STRUCTURAL DEFAULT, not independently recorded for this ASIN: `brandInCopy: false` — every Gildan-blank fixture in this codebase (blankSpecs.ts's own Gildan rows; every writer probe built on a Gildan blank) carries this value, because Gildan does not print its own name on the garment; called out here rather than silently assumed.

RULING N3 (round N, phase-n1-rulings.md, Blocking — closing review phase-m1-review-wire.md's BLOCKING 1, the THIRD consecutive round in which an undeclared fixture field moved the headline). `ihSpecFactFillers` (`productDetailAttrs.ts:516-523`, `IH_PAD_FILLER_DESCRIPTORS`) reads SIX descriptors — `material`, `fit`, `unisex`, `neck`, `sleeve`, `dye` — and this fixture's `blank` carried only the first three, silently omitting the other three rather than recording them present-or-absent. Two of the three missing fields ARE recorded, in this SAME fixture, in fields the round that added them never cross-checked against the blank: `neck: "Crew Neck"` is the blank's own recorded fabric/construction citation two paragraphs up ('Gildan 18000, 50/50 (cotton/polyester) CREWNECK, Classic fit' — RULING K4, `phase-k1-rulings.md:86`, 'Blank: Gildan 18000, 50/50 crewneck, Classic fit, lean_female'), and `sleeve: "Long Sleeve"` is named in this fixture's OWN `titleTemplate` field, added the SAME round M5 that left the blank incomplete ('THE CEO {design} Sweatshirt | LONG SLEEVE Pullover Crewneck'). Both are now added to `blank` above, sourced from those two citations, never invented. `dye` is genuinely NOT recorded for this blank anywhere in this repo's artefacts — Gildan 18000 is not associated with a documented dye process in any cited record — and is correctly left absent rather than guessed; `ihSpecFactFillers` treats an absent field as contributing no filler, exactly as designed. Measured effect (`w4-blankfields.probe.ts`, re-run against this corrected fixture): the derived `specFacts` gains further entries (RULING O4, round O, phase-o1-rulings.md — this paragraph's own prior wording, "a fourth entry" and its naive-join character count, was itself wrong, a defect named and closed by RULING O4, not retyped correctly here either — the exact `specFacts` length and naive-join length are pinned in the fixture test and read from that test's own logged output), clearing DQG's own grammar-constrained search where it previously found zero candidates — DQG's accept status is likewise read from the fixture test's own log, never hand-typed in this note again (see RULING N4 for the DQG mechanism this replaces).
